Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write an incident report for a two-hour outage of a payment API caused by a expired TLS certificate. Around 200 words.

Payment API Outage

2026-09-03-001 · 14:32–16:32 UTC (2 hours) · Critical

At 14:25 UTC on September 3, the TLS certificate on the payment API's primary endpoint expired. The system had no alerting mechanism for certificate expiration, so the failure went undetected until customer traffic began hitting SSL validation errors at 14:32 UTC. Approximately 8,400 transactions failed during the outage window. Customers received payment errors; no funds were charged or lost, but transaction processing halted entirely.

The root cause traced to August 28, when a replacement certificate was issued but never deployed to production. The deployment checklist included a required verification step that was skipped, leaving the expired certificate running.

On-call identified the issue at 15:10 UTC. A new certificate was deployed by 16:18 UTC, restoring the API at 16:32 UTC.

To prevent recurrence, certificate expiration alerting will activate 30 days before renewal, and certificate renewal verification will be added to the pre-release checklist.

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Add a section on what will stop it recurring.

Prevention

Two gaps created this outage: the absence of expiration alerting, and a deployment step that was skipped. Both are now addressed.

Automated alerting will trigger 30 days before each certificate expires, routing to the on-call engineer. This provides a buffer to renew and deploy before the certificate becomes invalid.

Certificate renewal verification is now a required step in the deployment checklist. After deployment, the API will run an automated test that confirms the new certificate is active and will not expire within 7 days. Deployments that fail this check will not progress to production.

Additionally, a weekly monitoring job will scan all certificates in the infrastructure and surface any that expire within 60 days, catching gaps that scheduled renewal might miss.
